p: One of the best things about clipping on at Coombe is the company it keeps. Warwickshire is castle country, and two of the big names are a short drive away. Kenilworth Castle, the dramatic red-sandstone ruin looked after by English Heritage, is ideal for a wander and a picnic. Warwick Castle, with its towers, ramparts and shows, makes a full day in its own right, so you might save it for the next morning.

Nature fans have options too. Ryton Pools Country Park on the south side of Coventry has lakes and woodland walks, and Brandon Marsh, the Warwickshire Wildlife Trust nature reserve, is a lovely, quiet spot for birdwatching with hides overlooking the pools.

On the course itself, a couple of hours is a sensible estimate, plus time for kit and the briefing. Keep snacks and drinks in the car for afterwards and pop a spare top in your bag, as the woods can feel a good few degrees cooler than the car park. If you've got a nervous climber in the group, let them go second, so they can watch how someone else tackles each crossing first.

Coombe also has a well-known heronry by the pool, so keep an eye out for those big grey birds if you're walking round afterwards. It's a reminder that this place is as much about wildlife as it is about adrenaline.
